summary.executive_summary: This Placement Policy outlines the governance, eligibility criteria, and operational framework for student recruitment and internship activities at RV University. It establishes the Career & Alumni Relations (CAR) department as the central authority for managing placement-related activities, including student eligibility, recruiter engagement, and offer management. The policy mandates strict adherence to procedural requirements, including offer acceptance protocols, documentation submission, and disciplinary mechanisms for non-compliance. It also reserves broad rights for the University to modify terms, withhold placement services, and impose additional conditions based on academic performance or disciplinary history.
key_points: CAR is the central authority for all placement and internship coordination at RV University.
Student eligibility is contingent upon meeting mandatory conditions, including having no backlogs and maintaining 80% attendance in pre-placement training.
The 'Offer Progression Rule' and 'Dream Offer Rule' define the hierarchy and limitations on accepting multiple job offers.
Students are required to report all off-campus offers to the School Chairperson or Placement Officer for record-keeping.
The University reserves the right to modify policy terms, withhold placement services, and impose disciplinary actions for violations.
All official communication regarding placements must occur through CAR-approved channels.
red_flags: Section 1.28 (University Rights): The University reserves the right to unilaterally modify placement rules and eligibility criteria, creating uncertainty for students.

Section 1.23 (Disciplinary Mechanism): The policy allows for the withholding of placement opportunities based on disciplinary referrals without clearly defined due process or appeal rights for the student.

Section 1.12 (Offer Progression Rule): The activation of certain opportunities is tied to a 40% placement threshold, which may unfairly restrict student options based on the performance of their peers.
favorable_clauses: Section 1.1 (Preamble): Establishes a commitment to facilitating fair and transparent placement opportunities for students.
Section 1.2 (Purpose): Defines the objective of standardizing processes, which provides a predictable framework for students to follow.
unusual_clauses: Section 1.10 (Base Offer Rule): Defines a student as having 'secured' an offer the moment their name appears in the final selection list, regardless of whether the student has formally accepted the offer.

Section 1.14 (Dual Selection Scenario): Imposes a restriction on students who are selected by two companies simultaneously, effectively forcing them to forfeit one opportunity based on internal CAR perspectives rather than student choice.
recommended_actions: Seek clarification on the specific due process and appeal procedures for students facing disciplinary action under Section 1.23.
Request a formal definition of 'institutional norms' to prevent arbitrary withholding of placement services under Section 1.28.
Advocate for a 'cooling-off' period or a formal withdrawal process that does not penalize students for declining offers that do not meet their career goals.
Ensure that the 'Offer Progression Rule' (Section 1.12) is applied transparently and that students are notified in real-time when thresholds are met.
Review the policy for compliance with the Indian Contract Act, 1872, specifically regarding the enforceability of 'forced' offer acceptance.
